thread:
priya: Heads-up — trying to get the new CLI in pipx during onboarding and it fails on our Linux builders but works on my mac. Anyone seen this interaction between pipx + poetry-exported constraints?

priya: Repro steps: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --output requirements.txt --without-hashes` then `pipx install --pip-args='-r requirements.txt' ./dist/redwood_cli-0.7.0-py3-none-any.whl` -> fails during wheel build for cryptography.

priya: Error snippet: 
```
Collecting cryptography
  Using cached cryptography-40.0.2.tar.gz (500 kB)
  Preparing metadata (pyproject.toml) ... error
  ERROR: Could not build wheels for cryptography, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects
```

tom: ugh. CI images are debian slim with no rust toolchain and no libssl-dev usually. cryptography wheels should be manylinux though.. are you forcing source build?

priya: I think constraints.txt includes a platform-incompatible package pin. When pipx runs in the isolated venv it respects the `--requirement` file, and that file pins `cryptography==40.0.2` (which on this runner expects a wheel but falls back to sdist). Works on mac because prebuilt wheel available for macos arch we tested on.

alex: Can you paste the top of requirements.txt? sometimes poetry export adds markers like `cryptography==40.0.2; platform_system == "Darwin"` and pip interprets it differently in the env.

priya: snippet from requirements.txt: 
```
cryptography==40.0.2 ; python_version >= "3.8"
cffi==1.16.0
redwood-sdk==1.4.2
# via poetry
```

maria: two possible issues: 1) manylinux wheel not available for the runner's glibc (old distro) -> sdist build triggers rust requirement; 2) pipx (--pip-args) + constraints exported without platform markers might force a source build. Quick test: try `pip install --only-binary=:all: cryptography==40.0.2` inside a fresh venv to see if wheel exists.

priya: tried that — `pip install --only-binary=:all: cryptography==40.0.2` fails with "No matching distribution found" on CI. So likely wheel not available for that linux.

alex: workaround: vendor prebuilt wheel or upgrade runner to newer manylinux stacks. But for onboarding we want a robust flow: suggestion: publish a platform-agnostic binary wheel for redwood_cli that avoids pulling heavy C deps at install time (move cryptography to extras or runtime dependency in a separate package).

maria: Agree. Another option: change export step to include `--platform` markers and produce per-platform requirement files, or use `pip download` on a builder to collect wheels and lay them out for pipx `--pip-args`. Not great for public onboarding though.

priya: For now I hacked around by building a thin wheel in CI that pins cryptography to 38.x which had manylinux support on that runner. Not ideal. Filing a DX follow-up to standardize a reproducible installer that doesn't cause pipx pain.

priya: Also saw weirdness when users do `poetry install` locally then `pipx install .` — editable vs wheel confusion. Pipx expects a distribution; if devs run `poetry build` then `pipx install dist/...` it's fine. But `pipx install --spec .` sometimes grabs the repo and runs `pip` inside and ends up compiling sdists.

tom: Maybe doc change: recommended onboarding path: python -m venv && pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel && pipx install --pip-args='--only-binary=:all:' dist/redwood_cli-*.whl — plus a note about linux runner requirements.

alex: Filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/issues/512 with recommended fixes (split heavy deps, CI runner upgrade).

ci-bot: Build #3421 failed on ubuntu-20.04: cryptography wheel not found -> fell back to sdist -> missing rustc -> install aborted.

maria: thanks for the triage @priya. I'll follow up on packaging choices in next devex sync and propose a packaging policy to avoid heavy C deps in common onboarding path. :thumbsup:

priya: thanks all — will update the onboarding doc and link the GH issue in our quickstart.
